gaps.finding: No securely dated study work after 1934. No decorative object has a source earliest date after 1934.
gaps.action: Future targeted institutional permissions or licensed collections are needed for postwar and contemporary painting. Onchi's uncertain range does not fill this gap.

gaps.finding: Two Roman Egyptian funerary portraits and one Ethiopian Orthodox diptych. No West, Central, southern or Maghrebi painting traditions are sampled.
gaps.action: Seek verified rights and specialist metadata for further African traditions. A Deccani image of an African musician does not repair this maker/tradition gap.

gaps.finding: No Indigenous Pacific authorship or Southeast Asian painting tradition. Gauguin is a European painter working in colonial Tahiti.
gaps.action: Target appropriately documented collections; Gauguin is not a substitute.

gaps.finding: Seven works across Mexican, Brazilian and Uruguayan contexts, including one precolonial Teotihuacan fragment. Other regions and Indigenous traditions remain thin.
gaps.action: Keep specific contexts separate. The current decorative collection does not supply a verified Latin American expansion.

gaps.finding: Eight works by six known women makers; several landmarks depict caregiving.
gaps.action: Consider the existing Vallayer-Coster, Vigee-LeBrun and Beers works before adding another generic European male portrait.

gaps.finding: Only five high-abstraction descriptors and four low-complexity descriptors. Figurative, dense and atmospheric pictures dominate.
gaps.action: Use the reserved Black Square and Klee checks. Future additions should broaden sparse/abstract contrasts without equating modernism, Europe and geometry.

gaps.finding: Most known makers have one work. Many traditions have one object and one format.
gaps.action: Use the same-artist and within-tradition near-matches. Broad explanations need repeat support in independent tasks and distinct makers.

gaps.finding: Print, panel, canvas, fresco fragment, screen, triptych and scroll are scaled digital images.
gaps.action: Record display size, crop and detail access. Screen-scale complexity and photographed colour remain alternative explanations.

gaps.finding: The collection comes largely from museum open access and an editorial landmark canon. Europe and the later nineteenth century are overrepresented.
gaps.action: Describe the profile as choices within this curated set. More paintings from the same first-1000 CMA query will not make it representative of world art or public familiarity.

selectionRules: The opening uses four landmarks. Other main preference panels have at most two, with lesser-known specific counterexamples.
Ranking pairs from one task are dependent evidence.
WHY means a tentative explanation consistent with choices, not an internal causal reading.
Keep liking, interest, affect, self-reported recognition and stated reasons separate.
Reservations cover first preference ratings, not all visual exposure.
Country/context, era and artist selection are not personality, national identity, religion, politics or morality.
Approximate crosses on panels 5, 6 and 12 are designed comparisons with documented confounds, not causal experiments.
Original humanity means visible human-figure salience here, not virtue, kindness or humaneness.
Narrative, atmosphere and energy descriptors contain editorial judgement. Pixel palette is a property of the local reproduction, not original pigment or an emotional response.
Lesser-known culturally important works remain tradition anchors. Popularity is separate from quality and importance.
